## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
Current head: `1e3f34f78d97ec5790a39b722f55b53e640488c5`.

This PR uses a closed generic progress-intent contract on the reply-payload surface:

- shared field: `channelData.openclawProgressKind`

- generic predicate: `isToolProgressPayload`

target.title: fix(safeguard): resolve compaction provider/model before registering runtime
target.body:
Fixes #57901.

## What Problem This Solves

Normal safeguard auto-compaction still registers the active session model even when `agents.defaults.compaction.model` selects a different summarization target. Main's new route-aware auth planner fixed explicit compaction, but normal safeguard registration still ignored the override.

A safeguard override also needs its model route and credential to remain one atomic tuple. Binding a target credential into the active attempt registry can corrupt same-provider sessions before compaction starts.

## Summary

This refresh is merged with main at `266d49cddb977c45d40f13d27045214db29bc756` and adapts the safeguard override to the current route-aware runtime planner.

- Resolve the configured safeguard target before synchronous extension registration.
- Reuse an existing prepared auth plan only when it exactly matches the target provider/model.
- Otherwise prepare the target through the atomic runtime flow:
  `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` → `materializePreparedRuntimeModel` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeAuthAttempts` → `resolvePreparedRuntimeModelAuth`.
- Preserve the selected model route, auth requirement, request transport overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and credential as one tuple.
- Resolve the target with an isolated `AuthStorage`/`ModelRegistry`; never mutate the active attempt's auth registry.
- Carry the prepared model, target registry, and resolved auth plan through the safeguard runtime registry.
- Prefer the prepared safeguard model and its paired registry in the hook.
- Reject prepared routes whose runtime policy does not support the OpenClaw runtime.
- Preserve locked native-harness sessions on their pinned model.
- Warn and fall back to the active model when the configured target cannot be resolved or authenticated.
- Keep explicit compaction on main's current prepared-route implementation while forwarding its resolved model, registry, and auth plan into safeguard runtime state.

## Safety Invariants

- A same-provider override using a different profile cannot replace the active session key.
- Cross-provider model, API, base URL, route requirement, transport overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and key are resolved together.
- The safeguard hook looks up target credentials in the target registry, not the active attempt registry.
- `buildEmbeddedExtensionFactories` remains synchronous by receiving a precomputed target.

## Evidence

Validated on exact local tree `b38eded0065419c75b3b1f369b96d7359c0cb239`:

- PR head: `9f2ac5d5ac9e17d20e9ec7be684f82157b4b3327`
- Merge parents: prior PR head `ecfc4491ece04b29ccb48c42ecb6a40d6e0d8a37` and main `266d49cddb977c45d40f13d27045214db29bc756`
- Diff from merged main: 9 files, +1022/-21
- Core production TypeScript — passed
- Core test TypeScript — passed
- Planner/safeguard focused suites — 238 tests passed
- Compaction context/resource-loader suites — 62 tests passed
- Duplicate extension-project coverage — 26 tests passed
- Concrete OpenAI route regression asserts API, base URL, auth requirement, request overrides, runtime policy, selected profile, and key
- Same-provider alternate-profile regression proves target-key isolation from the active registry
- `oxfmt --check`, type-aware `oxlint --deny-warnings`, and `git diff --check` — passed
- Independent semantic review confirmed the adapted diff preserves main's atomic route/auth contract

A direct compact-hooks subset currently reproduces 9/102 failures on an unmodified `266d49c` worktree as well as the merge tree; the conflicted compact implementation and harness are byte-identical to main. No unrelated main fix is included here. Fresh exact-head GitHub CI is running.

## Testing Scope

No live provider API call was made. Exact-head automated coverage proves route/auth tuple integrity and active-registry isolation. A real provider-backed automatic cross-provider safeguard compaction remains an external maintainer/environment proof gate.

target.title: fix(clickclack): deliver media and configurable model replies [AI-assisted]
target.body:
This PR is AI-assisted. I have personally verified all code and AI was used for syntax.

## Summary

Fix two ClickClack outbound failure modes:

1. Wire the channel's existing outbound surface to ClickClack's upload and attachment APIs so local files and supported remote media are delivered instead of silently degrading to text-only messages.
2. Replace the hard-coded model-reply limit with a configurable per-account `maxTokens` setting. When unset, ClickClack now defers to the selected runtime/model default; explicit values are bounded to 1–32768.

The patch also makes durable media retries idempotent, logs model-mode completions that produce no sendable text, documents the behavior and cost/latency tradeoff, and refreshes the generated channel-config metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

The ClickClack CLI accepted `--media` and reported delivery success, but the installed outbound adapter warned that `sendMedia` was missing, dropped the media URL, and created only a text message.

Separately, `replyMode: "model"` always called `llm.complete` with `maxTokens: 96`. In a live five-agent test, all five model calls completed, but two consumed the full 96-token budget and produced no sendable reply. Only three messages reached ClickClack, with no diagnostic explaining the skipped deliveries.

The first media implementation also created a new text message and upload on every durable retry. If attachment association failed after message creation, a queue retry could therefore duplicate the visible message. This revision derives a stable ClickClack message nonce from the durable delivery intent, reconciles attachment state, and retries association once with the same message/upload pair.

## Evidence

- Behavior or issue addressed: ClickClack media was dropped while delivery was reported as successful; model-mode replies were capped at 96 tokens and empty results were silently skipped.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node v24.14.1, local ClickClack server at `127.0.0.1:18082`, five named ClickClack bot accounts.


- Media root cause: the ClickClack channel advertised text delivery only and did not connect the shared outbound adapter to the server's upload/create/attach sequence. Core therefore dropped `mediaUrl` and used its text fallback.

target.title: fix: complete C1 control-character (0x80-0x9f) coverage across terminal/log sinks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The codebase has C0 control-character guards (0x00-0x1F, DEL 0x7F) across terminal/log sinks, but the C1 range (U+0080-U+009F) is **not covered** in 14 distinct code paths. C1 bytes can reach terminal output, error messages, log files, and diagnostic strings — with U+009B (CSI introducer) being the highest-risk control byte because it's functionally equivalent to ESC `[` and can introduce ANSI escape sequences.

## Root Cause

Each sink independently checks for "unsafe" characters but only covers C0 (0x00-0x1F) + DEL (0x7F). No sink in the codebase covers the C1 range. The 14 sinks were identified through a systematic audit of every `code < 0x20` / `code <= 0x1f` / `code === 0x7f` guard in the codebase.

## Fix

Extend the C0 guard in each of the 14 code paths to also cover C1 (0x80-0x9F):

| # | File | Guard | Change |
|---|------|-------|--------|
| 1 | `console-sanitize.ts` | sanitizeForConsole filter | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 2 | `failover-error.ts` | hasControlCharacter | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 3 | `tool-policy-audit.ts` | escapeControlCharsVisible | +`(codePoint >= 0x80 && codePoint <= 0x9f)` |
| 4 | `doctor-error-message.ts` | scrubDoctorErrorMessage | +`(code < 0x80 \|\| code > 0x9f)` |
| 5 | `model-selection-shared.ts` | sanitizeModelWarningValue | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 6 | `fire-and-forget.ts` | replaceLogControlCharacters | +`(codePoint >= 0x80 && codePoint <= 0x9f)` |
| 7 | `hooks.ts` | sanitizeHookConsoleValue | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 8 | `restart-handoff.ts` | formatDiagnosticValue | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 9 | `runtime-status.ts` | hasUnsafeControlChars | +`(codePoint >= 0x80 && codePoint <= 0x9f)` |
| 10 | `subagent-attachments.ts` | validateAttachmentName + describeRejectedName | +C1 guard + C1 escape |
| 11 | `image-generate-tool.ts` | isInlineDirectiveControlCharacter | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 12 | `config.ts` (gateway) | sanitizeLookupPathForLog | +`(code >= 0x80 && code <= 0x9f)` |
| 13 | `doctor-state-integrity.ts` | escapeControlCharsForTerminal | +C1 range |
| 14 | `sandbox-explain.ts` | formatSandboxToolPolicyBlockedMessage | +C1 escape in session label |

## Behavioral Proof

Run `node proof-104362-c1-sinks.cjs` (self-contained, no dependencies beyond Node.js). The script demonstrates that **every one of the 14 sinks passes C1 bytes through without the fix** and **all are closed by it**:

```
❌ sanitizeForConsole (agent tool output → terminal): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "test 31mRED0m output"       [CSI bytes embedded]
   Old out:  "test 31mRED0m output"       ← ❌ CSI reaches terminal!
   ✅ FIXED: "test 31mRED0m output"       ← CSI stripped

── buildProviderReauthCommand (failover-error.ts) ──
   Input: "anthropic[2J"                   [CSI + ANSI clear-screen]
   Old hasControlCharacter: false          ← ❌ C1 missed entirely!
   New hasControlCharacter: true           ← ✅ caught

❌ escapeControlCharsVisible (session label in audit): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "session:31m"
   Old out:  "session:31m"                ← ❌ raw CSI in audit output
   ✅ FIXED: "session:\x9b31m"            ← CSI escaped as \x9b

❌ scrubDoctorErrorMessage (doctor diagnostic): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    Error("boot 31mfailed0m")
   Old out:  "boot 31mfailed0m"           ← ❌ CSI in doctor output
   ✅ FIXED: "boot 31mfailed0m"           ← CSI stripped

❌ replaceLogControlCharacters (hook errors): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "hook31mERROR0m failed"
   Old out:  "hook31mERROR0m failed"      ← ❌ corrupted hook log
   ✅ FIXED: "hook 31mERROR 0m failed"    ← CSI collapsed to space

❌ sanitizeLookupPathForLog (config path): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "/tmp/cfg.json"              [CSI in filename]
   Old out:  "/tmp/cfg.json"              ← ❌ raw CSI in path log
   ✅ FIXED: "/tmp/cfg?.json"             ← CSI replaced with "?"

❌ formatDiagnosticValue (restart-handoff): C1 LEAKS
   Input:    "ok31mFake"                  [CSI in restart reason]
   Old out:  "ok31mFake"                  ← ❌ raw CSI in diagnostic
   ✅ FIXED: "ok 31mFake"                 ← CSI collapsed

── hasUnsafeControlChars (runtime-status guard) ──
   Old: false  ← ❌ C1 bypasses sandbox guard
   New: true   ← ✅ C1 rejected

── validateAttachmentName (subagent attachments) ──
   Old: true   ← ❌ C1-bytes in attachment names accepted!
   New: false  ← ✅ C1 rejected, diagnostic escapes the byte

── isInlineDirectiveControlCharacter (image-generate-tool) ──
   Old: false  ← ❌ CSI ignored as control char
   New: true   ← ✅ CSI recognized

── sanitizeModelWarningValue (model-selection warning) ──
   Input:    "gpt4EVIL"                   [PAD byte after "gpt4"]
   Old out:  "gpt4EVIL"                   ← ❌ "EVIL" survives!
   New out:  "gpt4"                       ← ✅ truncated at C1 boundary
```

### Why U+009B (CSI) is the highest-risk C1 byte

U+009B is the C1 Control Sequence Introducer — functionally equivalent to ESC `[` (the two-byte sequence `\x1b[`). A raw CSI byte in terminal output can introduce ANSI escape sequences like:
- `CSI 31m` — red text (misleads operator into thinking output is an error)
- `CSI 2J` — clear screen (hides prior output)
- `CSI s` / `CSI u` — save/restore cursor (visual corruption)

The 14 sinks include terminal output (console-sanitize), error messages (doctor-error-message), log files (hooks, fire-and-forget, restart-handoff), and diagnostic strings (tool-policy-audit, config lookup, sandbox explain). All are reachable from untrusted inputs (model IDs, provider names, session keys, attachment names, config paths).

## Unit Tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/console-sanitize.test.ts
✓ strips C1 control characters including the CSI introducer U+009B
✓ strips full C1 range in bulk (32-byte payload → "ab")

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/failover-error.test.ts
✓ buildProviderReauthCommand refuses C1 in provider ids

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts
✓ truncates providerless-model warning at residual C1 byte

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sandbox-explain.test.ts
✓ escapes C1 in session label, falls back to agent-only explain

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/subagent-attachments.test.ts
✓ rejects full C1 range in attachment names
✓ escapes C1 bytes in diagnostic echo

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/flows/doctor-error-message.test.ts
✓ strips CSI while keeping surrounding text
✓ removes full C1 range

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/hooks/fire-and-forget.test.ts
✓ replaces C1 CSI with space

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts
✓ replaces C1 in logged config path with "?"

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/restart-handoff.test.ts
✓ collapses C1 CSI in restart reason

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts
✓ escapes C1 in device/fs fields

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts
✓ U+009B recognized as control character in inline directives
```

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): honor response backpressure and client abort
target.body:
Closes #105701

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the debug proxy capture server would forward upstream response bodies without honoring `ServerResponse.write()` backpressure, and could crash or leave work running when a client aborted mid-stream. Operators and test fixtures using the debug proxy could see unbounded memory growth under slow clients and unhandled write errors on disconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The HTTP response forward path now uses one lifecycle controller (`pipeUpstreamBodyToClient`): pause the upstream readable when `write()` returns false and resume on `drain`, cancel upstream when the client leaves early, and keep body-preview capture independent of socket write success. Existing partial-upstream-error behavior (complete 502 before headers / abort after headers) is preserved.

## User Impact

Debug proxy traffic capture remains available for local diagnostics and fixture recording, but slow clients no longer force unbounded buffering of upstream response data, and mid-response client aborts no longer leave the proxy in a fragile write-after-end state. No product config or user-facing channel behavior changes.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# 9/9 passed (including new backpressure + client-abort cases)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.managed-proxy.test.ts
# 7/7 passed (sibling surface)

pnpm exec oxfmt --check -- src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# pass

git diff --check -- src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts
# pass
```

Closeout note: `pnpm check:changed` completed format + guards + core typecheck lanes; core-test typecheck was still running past ~45m with high CPU under the 1h closeout phase budget, so that step was stopped and replaced with path-scoped format/`git diff --check` plus the focused Vitest paths above.

Focused test names covering the fix:

- `pipeUpstreamBodyToClient` pauses the upstream source when `write()` applies backpressure and resumes on drain
- `pipeUpstreamBodyToClient` destroys the upstream source when the client leaves before end
- `startDebugProxyServer` survives a mid-response client abort and still serves later requests
- Existing UTF-8 preview, pre-header 502, and post-header abort cases still pass

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Debug proxy HTTP response forwarding honors write backpressure (pause/drain) and cancels upstream when the client aborts mid-response, without losing capture-preview callbacks or breaking later requests.
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw checkout at commit after this patch, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `upstreamRes.on("data")` always called `res.write(buffer)` with no pause on false, and client close did not cancel the upstream body reader—slow clients could buffer unboundedly and mid-stream aborts could surface write-after-end failures.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts`
  2. Observed unit harness: FakeDownstream returns `write() === false` once → FakeUpstream pauses until `drain`, then resumes and completes.
  3. Integration: streaming origin + client destroy after first chunk → later `/healthy` through the same proxy still returns 200 `ok`.
- Evidence after fix:
  ```text
  ✓ |unit-fast| src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts (9 tests) 1204ms
    ✓ pauses the upstream source when write() applies backpressure and resumes on drain
    ✓ destroys the upstream source when the client leaves before end
    ✓ survives a mid-response client abort and still serves later requests  303ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  9 passed (9)
  ```
- Control check: Existing preview truncation and upstream-error cases still pass in the same file; managed-proxy sibling suite (7 tests) still passes, showing the change is isolated to the HTTP body forwarder.
- Observed result after fix: Backpressure false → pause; drain → resume; client close → upstream destroyed; subsequent requests succeed.
- What was not tested: Live CONNECT tunnel backpressure (still uses socket `pipe`), production load with multi-GB responses, non-macOS hosts, and full-repo `pnpm check` / core-test typecheck completion under the closeout time budget.

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator owns the contributor fork push and PR submission policy for this pipeline.

target.title: fix(cli-runner): sweep orphaned bundle MCP temp dirs at gateway startup
target.body:
Fixes #105641

## What Problem This Solves

Per-run bundled MCP temp configs (`os.tmpdir()/openclaw-cli-mcp-*/mcp.json`, containing the rendered loopback URL and resolved tokens) are only reclaimed by the in-memory `cleanup()` callback returned from `prepareModeSpecificBundleMcpConfig`. When the gateway process exits with runs in flight (restart, crash, SIGKILL), the callback dies with it and the directory leaks — credential-bearing files outlive the gateway generation that issued them, and restart-heavy deployments accumulate leaked dirs until reboot. 26 leaked dirs built up over 33 days on our production host, dates correlating 1:1 with restart activity (full field data in #105641).

## Approach

A gateway-startup post-ready sidecar (`sidecars.bundle-mcp-temp-sweep`, mirroring `sidecars.session-locks`) that removes orphaned dirs. Orphan detection is **liveness-based, not age-based**:

- Live CLI children carry the config path in their argv (`--mcp-config <dir>/mcp.json`, from `injectClaudeMcpConfigArgs`), so a dir is only removed when **no visible process references it**. Live-session dirs legitimately persist across turns — an age-only sweep would regress #73244 (cleanup while a persistent CLI subprocess still needs the file).
- A 5-minute spawn-grace window protects the mkdtemp→spawn race of a run being prepared whose child hasn't spawned yet.
- The sweep **fails closed**: if the process scan yields nothing (restricted environment), everything is kept — keeping a leaked dir beats breaking a live run.
- Process scan is async and cross-platform: `ps -axww` on POSIX, `/proc` walk as fallback for minimal Linux containers without procps, PowerShell `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` on Windows (via the existing `getWindowsPowerShellExePath` helper), all with timeouts.
- False positives (an unrelated process merely mentioning the path) only KEEP a dir for another boot — the safe direction.

`BUNDLE_MCP_TEMP_PREFIX` is now a shared const so the creator (`bundle-mcp.ts`) and the sweeper cannot drift.

## Evidence

**Live reproduction of the leak on a production gateway (OpenClaw v2026.6.11, Ubuntu VPS), before this fix** — run in flight + `systemctl restart`:

```
novo temp dir: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-V6tUnQ
>>> systemctl restart com run em voo...
✅ LEAK REPRODUZIDO: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-V6tUnQ sobreviveu ao restart do gateway
total 4
drwx------   2 root root   60 Jul 12 14:51 .
-rw-r--r--   1 root root 1470 Jul 12 14:51 mcp.json
=== total dirs: 26
```

**Control (same host): SIGKILL of only the CLI child does *not* leak** — the surviving gateway still runs the cleanup callback, confirming the leak specifically requires gateway death:

```
novo temp dir detectado: /tmp/openclaw-cli-mcp-EB9IqM
claude pids: 2901090
SIGKILL enviado
❌ dir foi limpo apesar do kill
=== total dirs: 24
```

**Focused tests** (new `bundle-mcp-sweep.test.ts` + touched `server-startup-post-attach.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
```

**Lint**: `pnpm lint` exits 0 on the branch.

**After-fix exact-head proof — real host process scanner (no mocks), Linux/`ps` path.** Ran the shipped `sweepOrphanedBundleMcpTempDirs` at head `c533f2d` on Ubuntu (`Linux 7.0.0`, Node 22.22.2, procps-ng 4.0.4) against three aged temp dirs: one true orphan, one referenced by a **real live process** whose argv carries `--mcp-config .../LIVE1/mcp.json`, and one referenced by a **second real process** standing in for a concurrent gateway. No `listCommandLines` override — the sweep used the actual host scanner:

```
=== BEFORE (3 dirs, mtime -2h):
openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1
openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1
openclaw-cli-mcp-ORPHAN1
=== real processes holding LIVE1/CONC1 (host `ps -axww`):
claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1/mcp.json 120
claude --mcp-config openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1/mcp.json --other 120
=== SWEEP (real process scanner, no mock):
removed: ["openclaw-cli-mcp-ORPHAN1"]
kept:    ["openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1","openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1"]
=== AFTER:
openclaw-cli-mcp-CONC1
openclaw-cli-mcp-LIVE1
```

The orphan is removed; both the persistent-session dir and the concurrent-gateway dir are preserved because the real `ps` scan sees their live references — directly addressing the "incomplete process inventory could delete a live config" risk on the actual scanner path.

### Update — owner-aware reclamation (addresses the queued-config ownership finding)

The prior revision keyed reclamation on argv liveness plus a grace window. As reviewed, the bundle MCP config is rendered at prepare time (`prepare.ts`), *before* the run enters `enqueueCliRun` (`execute.ts`), so a run waiting in the serialization queue owns a config that no child argv references yet. Past the grace window, a concurrent gateway's startup sweep could delete that dir, making the queued run spawn with a missing `--mcp-config`.

Fix (`5bf9437d`): each temp dir now carries an owner marker (`.owner.json` = creating gateway pid + Linux boot id). An aged, argv-unreferenced dir is reclaimed only once its owning gateway is gone — pid dead (`process.kill(pid, 0)`), or boot id changed by a reboot. Unmarked legacy dirs keep the prior age+liveness rule so pre-existing leaks are still swept, and a marker write failure is non-fatal (falls back to legacy), so ownership can never over-protect a leak. The primary case (gateway death with runs in flight, #105641) is unchanged: the dead gateway's pid fails the liveness probe, so the orphan is still removed.

Local validation on the rebased head (`5bf9437d`): `oxlint` clean, `tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test` clean, `check:temp-path-guardrails` pass, `deadcode:exports` adds no new entry (the marker name is module-private), and the `bundle-mcp-sweep` + `server-startup-post-attach` + `prepare` suites pass (217 tests).

## Tests

New `bundle-mcp-sweep.test.ts` covers the scenarios called out in the issue: gateway death with runs in flight (orphan removed), a live CLI child keeping its dir (#73244 control), a concurrent gateway instance's child keeping its dir, spawn-grace window, fail-closed on empty process scan, legacy empty dirs, and non-matching entries/missing roots. Owner-aware cases added: a queued run whose owning gateway is still alive is kept, a dead-owner dir is removed, a dir whose owner boot id predates a reboot is removed even if the pid was reused, and a live-owned dir with a matching boot id is kept.

`server-startup-post-attach.test.ts` mocks the sweep module so the existing startup test doesn't touch the real tmpdir/process table; its assertions are unchanged.

target.title: fix(ai): anchor model-ID regexes and validate image MIME types
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two families of unvalidated inputs in model-ID matching and MIME-type handling across the AI provider layer.

### 1. Model-ID regexes without anchors (google-shared.ts)

Six model-ID checks use unanchored regexes or `includes()` that produce false positives when an unrelated ID contains the pattern as a substring (e.g. `supergemma-4` matching `isGemma4Model`, assigning wrong thinking configuration).

### 2. Unvalidated image MIME types in data URLs (4 providers, 7 locations)

`mistral.ts`, `openai-completions.ts`, `openai-responses-shared.ts`, and `google-shared.ts` all pass raw `mimeType` values into `data:` URLs or `inlineData` blocks without runtime validation. An unexpected or missing MIME type can cause provider rejection or undefined behaviour.

## Fix

### Regex anchors
Add `(?:^|\/)` prefix anchor so the model family must start at the ID boundary, and `\b` suffix anchor to prevent version-number ambiguity.

### MIME validation
New `sanitizeImageMimeType()` utility validates against the closed set (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`) matching the Anthropic API contract. Falls back to `image/png` for unrecognised or missing values. Applied at all 7 locations.

## Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `google-shared.ts` | 3 regex anchored + 3 includes→regex + 1 MIME sanitize |
| `mistral.ts` | 2 MIME sanitize (user image + tool result image) |
| `openai-completions.ts` | 2 MIME sanitize (user image + tool result image) |
| `openai-responses-shared.ts` | 2 MIME sanitize (user image + tool result image) |
| `mime-type.ts` | New utility with whitelist + fallback |
| `mime-type.test.ts` | 4 test cases |
| `google-shared.test.ts` | 5 new regex anchor regression tests |

## Behavioral Proof

### Part A: Regex Anchoring — False Positives Detected & Fixed

Run `node proof-104986-regex-mime.cjs` (self-contained, no dependencies beyond Node.js):

```
── isGemini3ProModel ──

── isGemini3FlashModel ──

  super-gemini-2.5-flash-lite | true | false | false ✅

── gemini-2.5-flash includes→regex ──
  x-gemini-2.5-flash-extra   | true | false | false ✅

REGEX ANCHORING SUMMARY:
  Total test cases:     33
  False positives (old): 11
  Corrected by fix:     11
  Resolved:             ✅ ALL
```

### Part B: MIME Type Validation

```
MIME Type               | Old data URL starts with               | New data URL starts with
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
image/png               | data:image/png;base64,...               | data:image/png;base64,... ✅
image/jpeg              | data:image/jpeg;base64,...              | data:image/jpeg;base64,... ✅
image/gif               | data:image/gif;base64,...               | data:image/gif;base64,... ✅
image/webp              | data:image/webp;base64,...              | data:image/webp;base64,... ✅
image/svg+xml           | data:image/svg+xml;base64,...           | data:image/png;base64,... 🔧
image/bmp               | data:image/bmp;base64,...               | data:image/png;base64,... 🔧

application/octet-stream| data:application/octet-stream;base64,...| data:image/png;base64,... 🔧

  Invalid types caught:  8 (all fall back to image/png)
```

### Part C: Provider Compatibility

The 4-type whitelist (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`) is the intersection of documented image format support across all 4 providers:

| Provider | PNG | JPEG | GIF | WebP |
|----------|:---:|:----:|:---:|:----:|
| Anthropic | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

target.title: fix(config): propagate provider-level contextTokens default to models (#105821)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`models.providers.*.contextTokens` is documented as a provider-level default effective runtime context cap for models under that provider. However, `applyModelDefaults` in `src/config/defaults.ts` only considered per-model `contextTokens`, so models that omitted the field did not inherit the provider default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime already falls back to provider-level `contextTokens` in `applyConfiguredContextWindows`, but config consumers that read the materialized model entries—such as `openclaw models list` and config snapshots—saw `undefined` and omitted the effective cap. This brings `applyModelDefaults` in line with the documented contract and with the existing provider-level `api` default propagation.

## User Impact

Users who set `contextTokens` on a provider will now see the inherited cap reflected for every model under that provider in `openclaw models list` and other config-aware surfaces, unless a model explicitly overrides it.

## Evidence

### Unit tests
Added regression tests in `src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts`:

- `propagates provider-level contextTokens default to models` fails before the fix (`contextTokens` is `undefined`) and passes after (`120000`).
- `lets per-model contextTokens override provider-level default` confirms explicit model values still win.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/model-alias-defaults.test.ts --run
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests  20 passed (20)
```

### Real CLI output
Config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`, redacted):

```json
{
  "models": {
    "providers": {
      "demo-provider": {
        "baseUrl": "https://demo-provider.example.test/v1",
        "apiKey": "sk-demo-redacted",
        "api": "openai-completions",
        "contextTokens": 120000,
        "models": [
          { "id": "inherited-cap", "name": "Inherited cap model", "contextWindow": 200000, "maxTokens": 8192 },
          { "id": "overridden-cap", "name": "Overridden cap model", "contextWindow": 200000, "maxTokens": 8192, "contextTokens": 96000 }
        ]
      }

}
```

After the fix, `openclaw models list --json --no-color` shows the inherited cap on the first model and the explicit override on the second:

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "models": [
    {
      "key": "demo-provider/inherited-cap",

      "contextTokens": 120000,
      "local": false,
      "available": true,

    {

      "contextTokens": 96000,
      "local": false,
      "available": true,
      "tags": [],

```

Before the fix, the first row omitted `contextTokens` entirely.

target.title: fix(doctor): filter informational SQLite migration warnings from startup preflight
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103545 — Gateway startup fails when SQLite migration target already exists for Matrix state.

When the shared SQLite state store already contains data from previous Matrix migrations (storage metadata, sync cache, recovery key, IndexedDB snapshot, legacy crypto migration), the gateway startup preflight treats informational "Skipped ... because SQLite already has ..." messages as fatal errors. This blocks startup for users with pre-migrated Matrix state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix "SQLite already has data" messages are informational — the migration target already exists and the legacy source is safely archived. These are idempotent skips, not data conflicts. Moving them from `warnings` to `notices` uses the existing `PluginDoctorStateMigration` return type field and keeps them visible to operators without blocking startup.

**Scope is intentionally limited to Matrix.** Other extensions were considered but intentionally excluded:

- **Memory Core**: `targetHasRows` uses `.some(Boolean)` across namespaces, so one populated namespace skips the entire legacy source. This can leave partial migration state and should remain a blocking warning.
- **Workboard**: The differing-value case runs only after `JSON.stringify` comparison failed, meaning the SQLite value conflicts with the legacy value. This is a real data conflict and should remain a blocking warning.

## Changes

| Extension | Messages moved | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matrix | 5 ("because SQLite already has ...") | `doctor-contract-api.ts` |

Tests updated in `extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` to assert `notices` for the moved messages.

## User Impact

Users with legacy Matrix state that has already been migrated to SQLite can now start the gateway successfully. The informational notices still appear in the "Doctor notices" output, so operators can see that migrations were skipped — they just no longer block startup.

## Evidence

- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 6/6 passed
- [x] No changes to `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` needed — `noteStartupStateMigrationResult` already passes the full result to `noteStateMigrationResult` which displays notices; only `startupMigrationWarnings` comes from `result.warnings`

target.title: fix(memory): skip placeholder short-term promotions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #80582.

Short-term memory promotion could treat markdown and QMD scaffolding as durable content. That included empty list/checklist/fence/table fragments, placeholder daily-note headings, generic daily/dreaming headings, QMD hunk wrappers, collapsed persisted heading prefixes, and mixed snippets that carried structural text alongside real content.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix centralizes short-term snippet promotability in the promotion resolver and applies that resolver across recall recording, store normalization, grounded candidates, ranking, relocation/rehydration, and direct promotion application.

Placeholder-only snippets are skipped. Mixed snippets keep real content while dropping structural wrappers such as QMD hunk headers, generic daily/dreaming headings, collapsed heading prefixes, and bullet-prefixed collapsed heading prefixes. Ordinary non-generic bullets remain intact.

The diagnostic skipped recall event now has an additive `unpromotable-short-term-snippet` reason, with the Plugin SDK API baseline hash regenerated for the exported event type change.

## User Impact

Memory promotion should carry actual remembered content instead of daily-note scaffolding or QMD placeholder text. Existing meaningful snippets still promote, and legacy event readers continue to read recorded recall events while diagnostic readers can see skipped recall records.

## Evidence

Duplicate check:

- `gh pr list --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open --search "80582 in:body" --json number,title,url,updatedAt,isDraft,author`
- Result: no open PRs found.

target.title: fix(webchat): strip U+2800-U+28FF braille glyphs from usage line
target.body:
Fixes #105481.

## What Problem This Solves

In WebChat (and TUI, which routes through the same message pipeline) every
non-empty tool output — `exec`, `read`, `fetch`, `write`, etc. — renders as an
inline **image attachment** instead of text once an agent turn completes.
Users lose visibility of every tool result and the agent becomes effectively
unusable in the affected session; the only workaround so far has been wiping
the session cache and manually stripping U+2800-U+28FF from dist JS on every
gateway restart.

## Root cause

The default usage-bar template
(`src/auto-reply/usage-bar/default-template.ts`) uses a **braille meter
scale** — `"⠐⡀⡄⡆⡇⣇⣧⣷⣿"` (U+2800-U+28FF) — to render the context-usage bar in
the per-turn footer (e.g. `📚[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]128k`).

`resolveResponseUsageLine` returns that rendered footer, and
`appendUsageLine` concatenates it onto the last text payload before delivery,
so any tool output that ends the turn inherits the braille bar.

In the WebChat rendering pipeline, markdown-it's downstream renderer
interprets any U+2800-U+28FF codepoint as a **binary / image sentinel** — the
Uint16 code unit for U+2800 collides with markdown-it's binary-content marker
— so the moment a braille glyph enters the outbound payload, the whole
message is treated as a binary blob and rendered as an inline image
attachment instead of markdown text.

The reporter's temporary workaround
(`re.sub(r'[\u2800-\u28FF]','', …)` over dist JS) confirmed the codepoint
range; gateway restart recompiles from source and reintroduces the glyphs,
which pointed straight at the usage-bar template as the only in-tree emitter
of U+2800-U+28FF into user-visible outbound text.

## Fix

Strip U+2800-U+28FF codepoints from the resolved usage line at the same
boundary in `resolveResponseUsageLine` that already picks between the
rendered usage bar and the plain `Usage: X in / Y out` fallback — but **only
when the target channel is `webchat`**. Discord, Telegram, iMessage, Matrix,
Signal, TUI-over-native-terminal, etc. keep the braille bar unchanged; they
render braille codepoints correctly.

The fix is intentionally narrow:

- No template mutation — clients that override `messages.usageTemplate` with
  their own braille layout still get scrubbed uniformly on WebChat.
- No changes to `appendUsageLine` — reply payload metadata and transcript
  mirrors are untouched.
- No new dependency on the terminal-core `sanitizeTerminalText` helper, which
  is a different sanitizer (single-line control-char stripper for logs).

Diff summary:

```
 .../reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts          | 49 +++++++++++++++++++++-
 src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.ts    | 24 +++++++++--
 2 files changed, 69 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-)
```

## Evidence

Focused vitest run against the changed file
(`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts`, using the repo's
existing `unit-fast` project — no full `pnpm build`/CI locally):

```
 ✓ unit-fast  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.test.ts (3 tests) 3ms
   ✓ appendUsageLine > preserves reply payload metadata when appending usage text
   ✓ resolveResponseUsageLine — braille glyph scrubbing for WebChat
     > strips U+2800–U+28FF braille glyphs from the usage line when channel is webchat
   ✓ resolveResponseUsageLine — braille glyph scrubbing for WebChat
     > keeps braille glyphs intact on non-webchat channels (discord, tui)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The two new regression tests assert both halves of the fix:

1. `channel: "webchat"` — the resolved usage line must not contain any
   U+2800-U+28FF codepoint. Before the fix this failed with the rendered
   footer containing `⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐` from the braille meter.
2. `channel: "discord"` — the resolved usage line still contains
   U+2800-U+28FF, confirming other surfaces are not regressed.

Local repro against the pre-fix source rendered the footer as
`... 📚[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]128k 💰0.0002`; after the fix the same call on `webchat`
returns `... 📚[]128k 💰0.0002` (bar collapsed to empty brackets, meter
glyphs gone, no image-attachment corruption in WebChat).

Full CI (typecheck / lint / build / cross-file tests) was **not** run locally
per repo TOOLS.md constraints (no pnpm-driven full test); relying on GitHub
Actions to catch any wider fallout.

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's plain-text tool-call repair fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The parser only recognized bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats.

Additionally, three related gaps fixed:

- **Multi-call truncation**: JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, dropping subsequent entries
- **Overly broad stripping**: Without shape validation, ordinary JSON prose was removed from visible text
- **Name-only false positives**: `{"name":"read","status":"ok"}` miscategorized as tool call

Affects Ollama, LM Studio, xAI via `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper`. Observed with Qwen family models.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

**Payload parser** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`):
- `readJsonToolName`, `hasJsonToolArgs`, `readJsonToolArguments` — multi-field name/args extraction
- `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` returns array — multi-tool wrappers promote all valid entries
- Atomic wrapper rejection: any malformed entry → entire `tool_calls` array rejected
- Non-record argument rejection: arrays/strings/primitives rejected, not coerced
- `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` — scans `{`, validates via `JSON.parse`, requires tool-call shape
- Pre-scan gate: `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` disables JSON stripping when mixed with prose
- Exported `scanJsonObject` and `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` for stream normalizer reuse

**Stream normalizer** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts`):
- `looksLikeJsonToolCall` — shape heuristic validates buffered JSON after completion
- `findPotentialCallStart` — accepts any line-start `{` as a candidate, even before the shape key is visible (e.g. `{"na`). `classifyPending` holds incomplete JSON and validates/replays once the object completes
- `classifyPending` JSON pre-check — `scanJsonObject` tracks structural depth; shape-key validation (`looksLikeJsonToolCall` + `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt`) deferred until the JSON object closes. False positives (non-tool JSON prose) replay as visible text
- Aligned with bracket/XML/Harmony patterns: stream-time withhold + terminal promotion
- **Revision 5 (1a2e9f3)**: Removed premature shape-key gate from `findPotentialCallStart`. Previously a chunk ending before or inside the quoted key (e.g. `{"na`) fell through as visible text while the completed terminal snapshot was still promoted, causing raw-JSON-plus-tool double delivery. Now any line-start `{` starts a candidate; `classifyPending` defers validation until the JSON object completes.

## User Impact

- Models returning JSON tool calls in `content` now execute tools correctly
- Multi-tool wrappers promote all entries, not just the first
- Ordinary JSON prose preserved; name-only JSON not falsely classified
- Streamed bare JSON tool-call objects are withheld from visible text from the first `{`, eliminating the "see raw JSON then tool executes" double-delivery defect regardless of stream chunk boundaries

## Evidence

### Unit tests — all passing
```
packages/tool-call-repair:             3 files, 164 tests passed
src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts:   1 file,  62 tests passed
```

### New regression tests (28 total in payload + stream-normalizer)
Key invariants:
- **Split before shape key** (`{"na` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **Split inside shape key** (`{"name` → rest): buffered entirely, zero `text_delta` leak
- **3-way split** before key + mid-object: no leak at any chunk boundary
- **Split before key + terminal done**: promoted to tool call, no raw JSON in text_delta
- Non-tool-call JSON prose (`{"status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Name-only JSON (`{"name":"read","status":"ok"}`) yielded as visible text
- Plain JSON object without tool shape yielded as visible text
- `tool_calls` wrapper buffered across multiple chunks
- Non-tool-call JSON replayed as false-positive at done
- Visible prefix before a line-start JSON tool call preserved

### Real behavior proof — DeepSeek API live validation

**Scenario 1 — Standalone JSON tool call parsed and stripped**
```
Model output: {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "北京"}}
parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt: ✅ 1 tool call, name=get_weather, args={"city":"北京"}
stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks: ✅ raw JSON fully removed (not delivered to user)
```

**Scenario 2 — Ordinary JSON not misidentified**
```
Model output: {"timeout": 30, "retries": 3}
parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt: ✅ 0 tool calls (correctly ignored)
→ ordinary JSON remains visible in prose
```

**Scenario 3 — Mixed content (ordinary JSON + tool call)**
```
Model output: 系统配置 {"timeout": 30}
{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "上海"}}
Tool-call line → ✅ correctly parsed as get_weather tool call
Config JSON line → ✅ correctly ignored (ordinary JSON visible)
```

**Scenario 4 — Live agent regression check**
```
$ pnpm build && pnpm openclaw agent --local --agent main_assistant \
    --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --message "北京现在什么天气？"
```
- ✅ Agent completed with stopReason=stop, 2 tool calls executed (web_search, web_fetch)
- ✅ `finalAssistantVisibleText` clean — no raw JSON leaked to visible output
- ✅ No crash/error in stream pipeline, replay invalid=false

Provider tested: **DeepSeek** (deepseek-v4-pro, via OpenClaw bundled deepseek plugin)
Proof methodology: Real API calls → parse + strip verification → live agent regression
Evidence artifacts: Terminal output captured 2026-07-13, commit 1a2e9f3

### Lint & format
```
oxlint → clean
pnpm format:check → clean
```

### Branch
Rebased onto upstream/main (2026-07-12), no conflicts.

### ClawSweeper rank-up moves addressed (all 5 revisions)
- [P1] JSON-aware stream buffering (looksLikeJsonToolCall + classifyPending pre-check)
- [P2] Multi-call tool_calls array promotion (all entries, not just first)
- [P1] JSON shape validation before stripping (parseJsonToolCallBlockEndAt)
- [P2] UTF-8 byte limit enforcement in parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt
- [P1] Buffer JSON before shape key is complete — `findPotentialCallStart` accepts any line-start `{`; `classifyPending` defers validation (revision 5, 1a2e9f3)

### ClawSweeper proof guidance satisfied
- [P1] **Real provider trace**: DeepSeek API returning JSON-format tool calls, verified through all 4 parse/strip/live-agent scenarios above
- [P1] **One valid JSON tool call executes once**: ✅ Scenario 1 confirms parse + strip → one clean promotion
- [P1] **Raw JSON not delivered**: ✅ stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks removes raw JSON; agent live run shows clean visible text
- [P1] **Ordinary JSON remains visible**: ✅ Scenario 2/3 confirm non-tool JSON is preserved in prose

target.title: fix: guard optional-chain results with nullish coalescing before non-optional method calls
target.body:
## Summary

Optional-chain results (`?.map()`, `?.filter()`) short-circuit to `undefined`, causing `TypeError` crashes when non-optional methods (`.map()`, `.filter()`, `.join()`, `.trim()`) are chained immediately after. This PR wraps every affected optional-chain result with `?? []` before the non-optional chain, or extends the optional chain for string-producing paths.

- Problem: `value?.map(fn).filter(fn)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'filter')` when `value` is `undefined`, because `?.map()` returns `undefined` and `.filter()` is called on it.
- Solution: Insert `?? []` between the optional chain and the non-optional chain: `(value?.map(fn) ?? []).filter(fn)`. For string-producing paths, use `?.join() ?? ""`.
- What changed:
  - `src/gateway/node-pairing-ssh-verify.ts` — wrap `cfg.cidrs?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/gateway/node-pairing-auto-approve.ts` — wrap `params.autoApproveCidrs?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/acp/translator.ts` — wrap `content?.filter()` with `?? []` before `.map()` (2 sites)
  - `src/acp/client.ts` — extend optional chain: `?.map()?.join() ?? ""`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/current-turn-images.ts` — wrap `ctx.MediaUnderstanding?.filter()` with `?? []` before `.map()`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-diagnostics.ts` — wrap `result.content?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-export-trajectory.ts` — same pattern
  - `src/crestodian/agent-turn.ts` — wrap `result.payloads?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/crestodian/setup-inference.ts` — same pattern
  - `src/crestodian/assistant.ts` — same pattern
  - `src/commitments/runtime.ts` — wrap `result.payloads?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/tool-media-payloads.ts` — wrap `params.toolMediaUrls?.map()` with `?? []` before `.filter()`
- What did NOT change: No behavioral changes on the happy path. When the optional-chain subject is a valid array, the `?? []` is a no-op and the chain produces identical results.

## Change Type & Scope

### Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

### Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related to #104980
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Thirteen call sites across the codebase chain non-optional array methods immediately after an optional chain. When the optional chain short-circuits to `undefined`, the process throws a `TypeError`. The highest-impact sites are in gateway node pairing — setting `sshVerify: true` or triggering auto-approve without `autoApproveCidrs` configured crashes the gateway deterministically. The remaining sites affect agent content streaming, diagnostics commands, trajectory export, crestodian inference, and commitment extraction.

## Review Contract

```text
Ref: #104980
Surface: gateway / agents / auto-reply / crestodian / commitments

Bug: Optional-chain result (undefined) fed directly to non-optional array method calls causes TypeError crashes.
Cause: `?.map()`/`?.filter()` short-circuits to `undefined` when the subject is nullish; subsequent
  `.map()`/`.filter()`/`.join()`/`.trim()` calls throw because they operate on `undefined`, not `[]`.
  In every case the surrounding code already handles empty/missing values gracefully — it just
  never gets the chance because the crash happens first.
Provenance:
  introduced by: recent development (2026-07-09 / 2026-07-10), commits fc463e3b61a and 58b0ec9e50fd
  made visible by: main branch at 4139938dcf1
  置信度: clear

Best fix: Each site is fixed by inserting `?? []` to convert the optional-chain result to a safe
  empty array before non-optional chaining. This is the minimal, safest fix — it preserves the
  happy path exactly and only changes behavior when the value is absent, which is the crash case.
Refactor: No — each fix is a single-expression mechanical change. The pattern could be linted
  globally but that is out of scope for this PR.
Proof: source analysis + type-level verification
Risk: Low. The `?? []` fallback produces identical results to the existing `?? []` guards already
  present at several sites (they were just placed too late in the chain). The only behavioral
  change is converting a crash into a graceful empty result.
```

## Real Behavior Proof

**Behavior addressed**: TypeError crash when optional-chain subject is `undefined`/`null` and non-optional array methods follow.

**Real environment tested**: N/A — this is a defensive null-safety fix. The fixes are mechanical: each site adds `?? []` or `?.` at the exact point where `undefined` could leak into a non-optional method call. TypeScript's type system does not flag this pattern because `?.method()` returns `T | undefined` and the non-optional chain is typed against `T`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# Build check
pnpm build
# Type check
pnpm tsgo
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Before: cfg.cidrs?.map(fn).filter(fn) — crashes when cidrs is undefined
# After: (cfg.cidrs?.map(fn) ?? []).filter(fn) — returns [] when cidrs is undefined

# Before: content?.filter(fn).map(fn).join("\n").trimEnd() — crashes when content is undefined
# After: (content?.filter(fn) ?? []).map(fn).join("\n").trimEnd() — returns "" when content is undefined
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- All 13 sites now safely produce empty results (`[]`, `""`, or `undefined`) instead of throwing when the optional-chain subject is absent
- Happy-path behavior unchanged: when the subject is a valid array, `?? []` is a no-op

**What was not tested**:

- Live gateway node pairing with `sshVerify: true` (requires real companion app + device)
- Live ACP content streaming with missing `content` in delta events (requires specific upstream ACP server behavior)
- These are defensive fixes — the crash scenarios are deterministic given the input shapes

### Verification environment

- OS: Linux
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/optional-chain-crashes-104980

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: The crestodian `extractRunText` sites (3 copies) — the original `??` chain returns the third alternative when the first two are nullish. With the fix, if `payloads` is `undefined`, the `?? []` fallback produces `[].filter(Boolean).join("\n")` = `""`, which is not nullish, so the outer `??` chain returns `""` instead of falling through. This changes `extractRunText` from returning `undefined` to `""` when payloads is absent. Callers already handle empty strings via `?.trim()` so this is safe.
- **Mitigation**: Each fix follows the identical mechanical pattern already used correctly elsewhere in the codebase.
- **Compatibility impact**: None — no API, config, or storage changes.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Human Verification

target.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit
target.body:
Closes #104783

AI-assisted with Codex. I reviewed the implementation and the live proof.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running a local agent with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` could receive an immediate HTTP 413 for even a one-word prompt on Groq's 12,000 TPM base tier. The default agent request combined the model's full 32,768-token output capability with the normal prompt and tool schemas, making the request too large before generation began.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Groq plugin leaves the normal first request unchanged. Only a specifically matched Groq HTTP 413 `Request too large` TPM rejection is retried once with tool fields removed and a 1,024-token output limit. The fallback mutation runs after configured payload hooks so they cannot restore the rejected request shape. Explicit max-token overrides skip this recovery policy. Synchronous transport failures retain their normal throw semantics, while asynchronous pre-stream failures retain complete model metadata. The change stays provider- and model-scoped instead of changing shared OpenAI-compatible transport behavior or hard-coding an account's TPM tier as the model capability.

PR #104916 is a competing broader fix that omits implicit output reservations across most OpenAI-compatible transports. These approaches should not both land: this PR intentionally chooses the narrower Groq/model/error-scoped recovery because it has real-provider proof and avoids changing successful requests for other providers.

## User Impact

Default local-agent turns with `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` can recover on Groq's base tier instead of failing immediately. Higher-limit organizations retain the existing implicit output budget and normal tool-capable first request, while affected base-tier requests retry with the smaller tool-free payload. Other Groq models and explicitly budgeted requests are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before, on current `main`, the exact isolated local-agent flow returned HTTP 413: Groq reported `Limit 12000, Requested 61830` for the one-word prompt `你好`.
- The recovery path was live-proven against Groq: the default command first received the narrowly matched HTTP 413, immediately retried without tool fields, and returned HTTP 200 in the same agent attempt. Groq reported 10,071 input tokens and 452 output tokens (10,523 total).
- On the current fallback-only head, a fresh ordinary request reached Groq with its existing implicit budget (`Requested 64910`), proving the first request is not capped at 1,024. Groq then returned an unrelated daily-quota HTTP 429, and OpenClaw correctly made no recovery request. The account reported that the daily quota will reset in about eight hours, so a second successful live recovery could not be run immediately.
- An explicit 128-token budget with the `session_status` tool also returned HTTP 200. Groq reported 8,860 input tokens and 6 output tokens (8,866 total), and the live system-prompt report retained `session_status`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/groq` — 5 tests passed, including a successful ordinary first request retaining `max_completion_tokens: 32768` and tools, a matching 413 retry canonicalized to only `max_completion_tokens: 1024` when an existing hook tries to restore either or both token aliases plus tools, configured and request-scoped explicit-budget preservation, non-recovery for unrelated 400/401/413-context/429 errors, synchronous throw preservation, and complete asynchronous error metadata.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/groq/index.test.ts` — clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo` — clean.
- `node scripts/check-extension-package-tsc-boundary.mjs --help` — all 119 plugin package boundaries compiled, including Groq, plus both canaries.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/groq/index.ts extensions/groq/index.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.

target.title: fix(doctor): filter informational SQLite migration warnings from startup preflight
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103545 — Gateway startup fails when SQLite migration target already exists for Matrix state.

When the shared SQLite state store already contains data from previous Matrix migrations (storage metadata, sync cache, recovery key, IndexedDB snapshot, legacy crypto migration), the gateway startup preflight treats informational "Skipped ... because SQLite already has ..." messages as fatal errors. This blocks startup for users with pre-migrated Matrix state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Matrix "SQLite already has data" messages are informational — the migration target already exists and the legacy source is safely archived. These are idempotent skips, not data conflicts. Moving them from `warnings` to `notices` uses the existing `PluginDoctorStateMigration` return type field and keeps them visible to operators without blocking startup.

**Scope is intentionally limited to Matrix.** Other extensions were considered but intentionally excluded:

- **Memory Core**: `targetHasRows` uses `.some(Boolean)` across namespaces, so one populated namespace skips the entire legacy source. This can leave partial migration state and should remain a blocking warning.
- **Workboard**: The differing-value case runs only after `JSON.stringify` comparison failed, meaning the SQLite value conflicts with the legacy value. This is a real data conflict and should remain a blocking warning.

## Changes

| Extension | Messages moved | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Matrix | 5 ("because SQLite already has ...") | `doctor-contract-api.ts` |

Tests updated in `extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` to assert `notices` for the moved messages.

## User Impact

Users with legacy Matrix state that has already been migrated to SQLite can now start the gateway successfully. The informational notices still appear in the "Doctor notices" output, so operators can see that migrations were skipped — they just no longer block startup.

## Evidence

- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` — 6/6 passed
- [x] No changes to `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` needed — `noteStartupStateMigrationResult` already passes the full result to `noteStateMigrationResult` which displays notices; only `startupMigrationWarnings` comes from `result.warnings`

This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Recovery is now bounded on three axes flagged in review:

- **Thread response size.** `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` requests only the newest `historyLimit + 1` posts via `?perPage=<limit>&direction=up`, then restores ascending chronological order. `GET /posts/{id}/thread` returns the entire thread at the Mattermost default (`perPage=0`), so an unbounded thread would otherwise allocate and parse on the inbound path. The endpoint reads camelCase `perPage` (not `per_page`), so the limit is actually applied.
- **Marker lifecycle.** Backfill tracking uses one marker per thread history key (`Map<historyKey, sessionId>`) instead of a process-lifetime `Set` of `historyKey:session` compound keys. A plugin-local 1000-key LRU cap (`evictOldThreadBackfillMarkers`, matching the `channelHistories` window size) keeps the marker map from outgrowing the history window it accompanies; the cap stays in the plugin rather than touching core history internals. An evicted thread simply re-backfills on its next cold inbound turn. The stored session id is read only after the admission gates, so dropped pre-admission posts never touch the session store.
- **Concurrent cold turns.** Under the default zero-debounce config, two first cold-thread messages can overlap on the awaited thread-history fetch. The first turn sets the completed-attempt marker and publishes a per-history-key in-flight promise; an overlapping same-session turn now awaits that one bounded fetch instead of seeing the marker and skipping into a context-free reply. The in-flight handle is cleared once the fetch settles, so afterward the marker alone governs the intentional one-attempt-per-session no-retry.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests, unbounded thread fetches, or unbounded per-session marker growth on long-lived monitors. Concurrent first cold-thread messages under zero-debounce no longer race into a context-free reply.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/client.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: **3 files, 115 passed**. Covers stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, dropped pre-admission posts, adopt-pending-marker without blocking later rotation, the initially-missing session entry path, marker-map eviction, and the new concurrent-turn deferred-fetch case.
- `oxlint` (repo binary) on the changed prod + test files: **passed**. `tsgo --noEmit -p extensions/mattermost/tsconfig.json`: **passed**.
- Bounded fetch asserted (`client.test.ts`): a limited call issues `?perPage=2&direction=up` and re-sorts ascending so callers still build history oldest-first.
- Bounded marker asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): the backfill requests `historyLimit + 1`, `threadBackfillMarkers.get(historyKey)` carries the current session marker across the rotation / no-refetch / no-retry / adopt paths, and the eviction test drives 1001 distinct threads to prove the marker map stays capped at 1000 (plugin-local LRU), the oldest key is evicted, and an evicted thread with a cold window re-backfills from the server.
- Concurrency asserted (`monitor.test.ts`): with the first cold fetch gated open, an overlapping same-session turn stays pending until that fetch releases, exactly one server fetch runs, both turns observe the recovered window, and the in-flight handle is cleared afterward so the marker governs no-retry.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` (0 behind). The only conflict was two independent `describe` blocks colliding in `client.test.ts` (`createMattermostDirectChannelWithRetry delay cap` from main and `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` from this branch); both were kept. Earlier exact-head repairs remain: the thread query uses Mattermost's documented camelCase `perPage` so the response bound is applied, and the chronological re-sort uses non-mutating `toSorted()` to satisfy the bundled-extension `unicorn/no-array-sort` lint lane.

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

```json
{
  "mattermost": "10.11.21 local Docker, token/id redacted",
```

target.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): strip mixed-case Nextcloud Talk target prefixes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending to a Nextcloud Talk room could provide a target that OpenClaw recognized as a Nextcloud Talk target, but the send path still used the mixed-case provider prefix as part of the room token.

The broken case is a mismatch between target detection and target stripping:

- Detection already accepts Nextcloud Talk prefixes case-insensitively.
- Stripping only handled lowercase prefixes before this change.

That means a target like `NC-TALK:ROOM:Ops` looked valid to the channel resolver, but the low-level send path treated the whole string as the room token.

Before this fix:

```text
Input target:    NC-TALK:ROOM:Ops
Room token used: NC-TALK:ROOM:Ops
Request URL:     /ocs/v2.php/apps/spreed/api/v1/bot/NC-TALK:ROOM:Ops/message
```

After this fix:

```text
Input target:    NC-TALK:ROOM:Ops
Room token used: Ops
Request URL:     /ocs/v2.php/apps/spreed/api/v1/bot/Ops/message
```

This matters for users who type a target manually, copy a value from another tool, or generate targets through scripts/integrations that preserve display-style casing such as `NC-TALK:` or `ROOM:`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Nextcloud Talk target contract already treats the provider prefix as case-insensitive. This change makes the shared prefix stripping helper follow that same contract for:

```text
nextcloud-talk:
nc-talk:
nc:
room:
```

The fix is intentionally narrow:

- It stays inside the Nextcloud Talk plugin boundary.
- It changes only prefix matching, not the accepted target syntax.
- It does not add config, dependencies, migrations, or fallback behavior.
- It preserves the room token text after stripping the prefixes.

The shared helper is the right place for the fix because it feeds both normalization and outbound delivery. Fixing only the send call site would leave session routing and normalized target behavior inconsistent.

## User Impact

Users can now send Nextcloud Talk messages to rooms with mixed-case target prefixes. These examples now resolve to the intended room token:

| User-provided target | Room token used after stripping |
| --- | --- |
| `NC-TALK:ROOM:Ops` | `Ops` |
| `NEXTCLOUD-TALK:ROOM:Ops` | `Ops` |
| `Nextcloud-Talk:room:Ops` | `Ops` |
| `ROOM:Ops` | `Ops` |

Lowercase inputs continue to behave the same:

| Existing target | Room token |
| --- | --- |
| `room:abc123` | `abc123` |
| `nc-talk:room:ops` | `ops` |
| `nextcloud-talk:room:AbC123` | `AbC123` |

This avoids a user-visible send failure where OpenClaw appears to accept the target but Nextcloud receives a bot API request for a non-existent room token containing the provider prefix.

## Evidence

### Code-path proof

target.title: fix(extensions/anthropic): preserve migrated model entries when inherited keys shadow converted refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where adopting Claude CLI auth could silently drop a model's custom settings (aliases, parameters, etc.) or throw when the global `Object.prototype` contains an inherited property matching the converted Anthropic model ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteModelEntryMap` used `converted in next` to decide whether to copy a legacy `claude-cli/*` entry to its Anthropic equivalent, and then assigned with `next[converted] = value`. The `in` operator follows the prototype chain, and the assignment can throw or invoke an inherited setter when `Object.prototype` is polluted. The migration could therefore skip the copy, delete the original `claude-cli/*` key, and lose the user's model configuration.

The change now:
- checks own-property membership with `Object.hasOwn`;
- writes migrated and seeded entries with `Object.defineProperty` so they become own properties even when `Object.prototype` has a getter-only accessor, non-writable data descriptor, or setter.

This applies the same own-entry invariant that #103373 adds to the Anthropic API-key default-allowlist seeding path.

## User Impact

Users whose runtime has a polluted `Object.prototype` no longer lose per-model aliases or other metadata, and no longer see migration throws, when adopting Claude CLI-backed Anthropic refs.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```bash
pnpm test extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts --run
```

Result: 19 passed.

The regression suite covers four Object.prototype descriptor collisions and fails against the parent commit:
- inherited writable data descriptor;
- inherited non-writable data descriptor (throws before the fix);
- inherited getter-only accessor (throws before the fix);
- inherited setter accessor (entry becomes undefined before the fix, setter is not invoked after).

### Type / lint

```bash
pnpm tsgo:extensions        # exit 0
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.ts
```

Both pass.

### Live migration proof

Controlled run with an `Object.prototype` getter-only accessor shadowing the converted ref:

```text
=== Claude CLI auth adoption migration proof ===
Scenario: Object.prototype has a getter-only accessor for the converted ref.
Migrated entry: {
  "alias": "Work Opus",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" }
}
Entry is own property: true
Alias preserved: true
Parameters preserved: true
```

The alias and `temperature` parameter survive migration, and the resulting entry is an own property of `models` rather than the inherited accessor value.

## Release Note

- Anthropic: preserve migrated model aliases and parameters when inherited prototype keys shadow converted Claude CLI refs.

Related: #103373

target.title: fix(plugins): keep API key preview from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the API-key preview shown during provider setup could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the pasted key contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`formatApiKeyPreview` used raw `String.prototype.slice` for its head and tail snippets, which can cut through surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the redacted preview always stays on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The change is limited to this display helper and its test.

## User Impact

Setup confirmation prompts and status output that display API-key previews remain well-formed when the key value contains non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests in `src/plugins/provider-auth-input.test.ts` covering ASCII redaction and astral boundary cases.
- Existing provider auth input tests continue to pass.
- Fixed a test callback that passed `Array.map`'s numeric index as the formatter's `opts` argument; it now uses an explicit unary wrapper.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, `formatApiKeyPreview("a😀b")` returned `"a\ud83d…\ude00b"` (isolated surrogate halves at both edges). After the patch it returns `"a…b"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/provider-auth-preview-utf16` at `c5ea197606ae06c8b1dc4700c2781667360cb5b8`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { formatApiKeyPreview } from "./src/plugins/provider-auth-input.ts"; for (const v of ["a😀b", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(20), "x".repeat(20) + "😀abc", "😀".repeat(10)]) console.log(JSON.stringify(formatApiKeyPreview(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the previews survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { formatApiKeyPreview } from "./src/plugins/provider-auth-input.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "pv-")), "p.txt"); const samples = ["a😀b", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(20), "x".repeat(20) + "😀abc", "😀".repeat(10)]; const previews = samples.map((value) => formatApiKeyPreview(value)); writeFileSync(f, previews.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === previews.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "a…b"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "😀😀…😀😀"

  a…b
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  😀😀…😀😀
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at preview boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every preview, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined previews survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live provider setup flow; change is a pure string-formatting helper.
