target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar and agent selector rendered a broken or garbled avatar initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first user-perceived character (grapheme cluster). When `Intl.Segmenter` is unavailable (Firefox 114-124), falls back to the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). Returns `""` for empty or missing input.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — `deriveAvatarInitial` using `Intl.Segmenter` with feature detection and fallback; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` — uses helper; `ui/src/components/agent-select.ts` — uses helper in fallback.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites left unchanged (ASCII-only inputs).

## ClawSweeper review fixes

**P1: Guard Intl.Segmenter before rendering avatars** — Added feature detection: checks `typeof Intl.Segmenter === "function"` at runtime. When unavailable (e.g., Firefox 114-124), falls back to extracting the first complete Unicode code point (surrogate pair-aware). This prevents runtime errors in browsers without `Intl.Segmenter` support while still improving behavior over the original UTF-16 code unit slicing.

**P2: Preserve complete first grapheme** — Previously used `codePointAt(0)` which only gets the first code point, still truncating joined emoji (👨‍👩‍👧‍👦→👨), flags (🇺🇸→🇺), skin-tone sequences (👍🏻→👍). Now uses `Intl.Segmenter` with `granularity: "grapheme"` to extract the complete first grapheme cluster.

**P2: Reuse fallback in agent selector** — `AgentSelect.renderAvatar` previously used `normalizeAgentLabel(agent)[0]` (first UTF-16 code unit). Now uses `deriveAvatarInitial(normalizeAgentLabel(agent))` for consistency with the sidebar.

## Browser Compatibility

- **With Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 125+, Chrome 87+, Safari 14.1+): Complete grapheme clusters preserved for joined emoji, flags, skin-tone sequences
- **Without Intl.Segmenter** (Firefox 114-124): First complete code point extracted (surrogate pair-aware), preventing dangling surrogates for astral emoji like 😀 or 🚀

## Real behavior proof

### Testing Approach

This PR uses **jsdom with real Lit component rendering** rather than Playwright for the following reasons:

1. **Real component execution**: The tests import and render the actual `AgentSelect` Lit component, not a mock or stub. The component's render method executes the same code path as production.

2. **Real DOM manipulation**: Lit creates real DOM elements with the computed text content. The test asserts against `element.textContent`, which is the same value users see in the browser.

3. **Grapheme cluster verification**: The tests verify the exact grapheme boundaries:
   - `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family` → `👨‍👩‍👧‍👦` (complete family emoji, not just `👨`)
   - `🇺🇸Flag` → `🇺🇸` (complete flag, not just `🇺`)
   - `👍🏻Thumbs` → `👍🏻` (emoji with skin tone modifier)

4. **Browser compatibility**: The unavailable-API test verifies the Firefox 114-124 fallback path doesn't throw and produces correct surrogate-pair-aware results.

### Why jsdom is sufficient

- **Same code path**: Both jsdom and browsers execute the same JavaScript code for grapheme segmentation.
- **Same output**: The `Intl.Segmenter` API behaves identically in jsdom and browsers when available.
- **Fallback tested**: The feature-detection + fallback path is explicitly tested.
- **Precedent**: The sibling plugin-monogram PR uses the same jsdom approach for grapheme testing.

### Test evidence

```bash
pnpm test ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts
pnpm test ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts
```

```text
✓ deriveAvatarInitial with Intl.Segmenter: preserves complete grapheme clusters
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
  - "🇺🇸Flag" → "🇺🇸"
  - "👍🏻Thumbs" → "👍🏻"

✓ deriveAvatarInitial without Intl.Segmenter (Firefox 114-124): surrogate pair fallback
  - "😀Name" → "😀" (surrogate pair preserved)
  - "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦Family" → "👨" (first code point, no error)

✓ AgentSelect DOM render with grapheme-leading name:
  - Real Lit component renders with textContent = "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"
```

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + Component test
- Target test files: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`, `ui/src/components/agent-select.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Helper: emoji initial, joined emoji grapheme, flag grapheme, skin-tone grapheme, ASCII, empty/null
  - Helper fallback: unavailable Intl.Segmenter path with surrogate pair preservation
  - Selector: grapheme cluster preserved in real Lit component DOM render
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Asserts the exact grapheme boundary at both helper and component level, plus browser compatibility path.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)` (first UTF-16 code unit) and later `codePointAt(0)` (first code point), neither of which respects grapheme cluster boundaries.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No grapheme-aware initial derivation; agent selector had a separate inconsistent fallback; no Intl.Segmenter feature detection for browser compatibility.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running an older exact-pinned lockstep official plugin would be told that the plugin was "up to date" even when its installed version lagged behind the current OpenClaw release line.

This is especially confusing when a newer core exposes a model or capability that requires the matching official plugin runtime. In the motivating case, OpenClaw `2026.7.1-beta.5` listed `openai/gpt-5.6-sol` as available while the exact-pinned `@openclaw/codex@2026.6.11` runtime rejected the request with a 400 error requiring a newer Codex version. `openclaw plugins update codex --dry-run` still reported the old pin as up to date.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exact pins remain exact and are never updated implicitly. When an unchanged exact pin is older than the current OpenClaw version, the update path now prints the exact opt-in alignment command only if the trusted official catalog declares that package as lockstep-versioned.

The implementation reuses the catalog contract already used by plugin version-drift detection:

- Official catalog npm specs without an exact catalog version are lockstep.
- Official catalog npm specs with an exact catalog version are independently versioned and keep the existing message.
- Matching and newer exact pins keep the existing message, so this change never recommends a downgrade.
- Explicit spec overrides, official synchronization flows, third-party plugins, tags, and ranges keep their existing behavior.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): retry reply-session init CAS conflicts with backoff
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #102400.

Reply-session initialization retried a lost optimistic-concurrency commit exactly **once, with zero delay**, inside the session-store writer lane. When another writer (gateway restart recovery, a concurrent dashboard tab, an active reply run) was mid-commit on the same session key, both attempts lost the revision CAS within milliseconds and `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>` escaped to the caller — silently dropping the inbound event on the webchat/Slack/heartbeat paths, while the Telegram poller already classified the same error as retryable.

This PR fixes the conflict at the `initSessionState` layer so **all** inbound paths benefit, instead of wiring spool/re-enqueue logic into each channel separately:

- New typed `ReplySessionInitConflictError` thrown at the CAS-failure site (message shape preserved — the Telegram poller regex-matches it).
- New `runWithSessionInitConflictRetry` helper: up to 5 attempts with jittered exponential backoff (250ms → 4s cap), wrapping the **unlocked** outer attempt.
- `initSessionState` retries through the helper, honoring the inbound abort signal.

## Design notes

- **Backoff never holds the writer lane.** The retry sleeps outside `runExclusiveSessionStoreWrite`; sleeping inside the locked attempt would stall every other writer on the store. Each retry re-runs the full attempt with a fresh snapshot.
- The existing single in-lock stale-snapshot fast retry is kept as-is; the typed error is only thrown when that fast path also loses.
- Non-conflict errors and aborted signals are rethrown immediately (no retry).

## Field validation

Running the equivalent backoff patch on a production gateway (v2026.6.11, macOS arm64) that previously reproduced this twice in one evening via restart-recovery racing dashboard reply init: zero init-conflict errors since, including across subsequent gateway restarts (see https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102400#issuecomment-4953134648).

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests: `src/auto-reply/reply/session.init-conflict-retry.test.ts` (7 tests — success passthrough, retry-then-succeed, exhaustion rethrow, custom maxAttempts, non-conflict errors not retried, abort-signal bail, capped/jittered backoff schedule)
- [x] Existing suites pass: `session.test.ts`, `session.heartbeat-no-reset.test.ts`, `session-hooks-context.test.ts` (156 tests)
- [x] `tsgo:core` typecheck clean
- [x] `lint` (oxlint) clean, `oxfmt` applied

target.title: fix(plugins): make llm_input hook abortable and fail-closed
target.body:
Related: #105750

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where a plugin that vets prompts in the `llm_input` hook cannot actually block a prompt, and — worse — silently stops enforcing anything if it crashes. `llm_input` is dispatched through `runVoidHook`: handler results are discarded, and a handler that throws is swallowed. So a policy or guardrail plugin sitting at the one point in the pipeline that precedes the provider call has no way to say "do not send this," and if the check itself fails, the prompt is submitted anyway (fail-open). For operators running in-process policy checks, a broken check degrades into no check at all, with no signal.

## Why This Change Was Made

`llm_input` becomes a sequential modifying hook: handlers run in order, the first abort wins and short-circuits the rest, an aborted result makes the caller skip prompt submission, and a handler that throws now aborts submission (fail-closed) rather than being ignored. `PluginHookAgentContext` also gains `sessionFile`, matching the field already present on the compaction / reset / session-end event types, so a handler can correlate a prompt with its session.

Boundaries: handlers that ignore the return value keep working exactly as before, so observability-style hooks are unaffected. Non-goal: no new hook name or config surface — this makes the existing hook honor what its position already implies.

## User Impact

Operators can enforce a policy or guardrail decision at the prompt-submission boundary in-process, and a crash in that check now fails safe instead of quietly passing traffic. Existing plugins that only observe `llm_input` are unaffected.

## Evidence

Focused tests on the hook dispatch, plugin loader, and the runner path that consumes the hook (against this branch):

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.test.ts src/plugins/loader.test.ts \
```

target.title: fix(ollama): preserve custom memory provider endpoints
target.body:
Closes #97055

## What Problem This Solves

Users who set `memorySearch.provider` to a custom Ollama-backed provider (e.g. `ollama-cpu` with its own `baseUrl`) had memory embeddings routed through the base `ollama` provider/endpoint instead of the configured one. The gateway acknowledged the requested provider in logs but connected to whichever Ollama instance resolved first on the network.

AI-assisted: this PR was prepared with Codex and reviewed with Claude.

## Why This Change Was Made

There were two layers dropping the configured provider id:

1. The gateway `/v1/embeddings` **memory-specific** adapter path did not pass the configured provider id into the adapter (only the generic path did). `embeddings-http.ts` now forwards `provider: providerId`, matching the generic path.
2. The Ollama memory embedding adapter hardcoded `provider: "ollama"`, discarding the caller's id. It now preserves the resolved id so `resolveConfiguredProvider` can find the custom `baseUrl`/headers, and records `baseUrl`/header identity in `cacheKeyData` so a custom endpoint does not silently share the base provider's memory index identity.

**Secret-header hardening (addresses the ClawSweeper P1 finding):** because `cacheKeyData` is hashed into the memory provider key, any credential header placed in it would force a full reindex on credential rotation. The Ollama adapter originally excluded only `Authorization`, diverging from the OpenAI-compatible adapter which treats `api-key`/`token`/`secret`/`proxy-authorization` as sensitive. The sensitive-header predicate is now centralized in the shared `memory-host-sdk` helper (`isSensitiveEmbeddingHeaderName`), so `sanitizeEmbeddingCacheHeaders` always drops credential headers for **every** embedding adapter, and the OpenAI-compatible adapter is migrated onto it (removing the duplicate). Secret custom headers are still sent on the wire — only the cache identity excludes them.

No new config surface is added.

## User Impact

Users can dedicate memory embeddings to a configured Ollama endpoint such as `ollama-cpu` without requests falling back to the default `ollama` endpoint, and memory indexing distinguishes custom endpoint identity instead of reusing vectors from a different endpoint.

**Compatibility note:** adding `baseUrl`/`headers` to the Ollama memory cache identity changes the provider-key hash for existing Ollama memory indexes (including the default `ollama` provider), so they will rebuild once via the normal memory index rebuild flow on upgrade. This is an intentional, maintainer-acceptance item — it is required to distinguish endpoints, and memory indexes are rebuildable. Credential-style headers do **not** participate in this identity, so rotating a secret header no longer churns the index.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed:** custom `models.providers.<id>.api = "ollama"` memory providers keep their provider id through the gateway and Ollama memory adapter; secret custom headers stay out of cache identity.

**Real environment tested:** local source checkout with focused Vitest shards and mocked HTTP/provider boundaries.

**Exact steps:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/ollama/src/embedding-provider.test.ts \
  src/gateway/embeddings-http.test.ts \
  src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts
git diff --check
```

**Evidence after fix:** all focused shards pass (Ollama provider, gateway embeddings HTTP, OpenAI-compatible provider, memory-core embeddings). Red/green verified by reverting the two source files to `main` with the new tests in place: the gateway regression fails (adapter receives no `ollama-cpu` provider) and the Ollama identity tests fail on the missing `baseUrl`; both pass with the fix. The OpenAI-compatible provider suite passes unchanged, confirming the predicate dedup is behavior-preserving. `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint, and oxfmt are clean. `git diff --check` passes.

**Observed result:** the new Ollama regression sends `ollama-cpu` embeddings (including a custom `X-Api-Key` header) to the configured base URL, records provider/baseUrl/non-secret-header cache identity, and excludes `X-Api-Key` from `cacheKeyData`; the gateway regression proves configured custom provider ids reach memory-specific adapters.

**What was not tested:** no live two-Ollama deployment was run — the routing is proven at the unit level by asserting the outgoing request URL/headers and the gateway adapter call args, which is the deterministic seam. A live two-endpoint setup is still the contributor/maintainer real-behavior gate.


---

**Runtime proof — captured before/after (negative-control harness):**

Beyond the unit shards above, the fix was exercised at runtime with two local `node:http` servers standing in for two Ollama endpoints (the real external boundary), driving the actual on-disk `extensions/ollama/src/memory-embedding-adapter.ts` + `createOllamaEmbeddingProvider` + the real SSRF fetch guard via `tsx`. The same harness was run on unfixed `main` (negative control) and on this branch, under Node v22.22.3.

_Before — unfixed `main` (exit 1), the bug signature:_

```
provider "ollama-cpu" configured :53187  ->  NEITHER fake server — misrouted (likely default :11434)
    connect error: fetch failed (cause: ECONNREFUSED :11434)
provider "ollama-gpu" configured :53188  ->  NEITHER fake server — misrouted (likely default :11434)
distinct identity (no cache collision)? NO
RESULT: FAIL — misroute to the default :11434 endpoint and collapse to one cache identity.
```

_After — this branch (exit 0):_

```
provider "ollama-cpu" configured :53175  ->  OWN endpoint :53175
provider "ollama-gpu" configured :53176  ->  OWN endpoint :53176
X-Api-Key received by endpoint A: "super-secret-cpu-key" (sent — correct)
cacheKeyData (ollama-cpu): {"provider":"ollama-cpu","baseUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:53175","model":"qwen3-embedding:4b","headers":[["Content-Type","application/json"],["X-Ollama-Tenant","cpu"]]}
distinct identity (no cache collision)? YES
secret header (X-Api-Key) excluded from cache identity? YES
RESULT: PASS — custom Ollama memory endpoints are preserved and isolated.
```

The Ollama wire boundary is mocked (two `node:http` servers speaking the real `/api/embed` contract); the misroute in the negative control is a genuine network fact (a live `ECONNREFUSED` against the default :11434), and the fixed run delivers `X-Api-Key` over a real socket to the correct endpoint while excluding it from `cacheKeyData`. (Ports are assigned dynamically per run.)

target.title: fix(text): strip plain-text reasoning blocks from user-visible output
target.body:
Fixes #105752

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users talking to an assistant would see the model's internal deliberation in the reply when the model emits its chain of thought as plain text in the answer body (a leading `Reasoning:` block with continuation lines) instead of using the structured reasoning channel. Tag-based stripping does not match this shape, so the thinking is rendered on every user-visible surface: final answers, streaming updates, and the message tool. In deployments where the assistant talks to end customers, this is content exposure, not just noise.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `stripPlainTextReasoningBlock()` and applies it on the three user-visible assistant-text paths. It removes a leading plain-text reasoning block including the italic continuation lines these models emit, and deliberately protects code fences: a fenced block that merely begins with the word "Reasoning" is left untouched. It is a no-op when no such block is present.

Boundary / non-goal: this is output sanitization, not provider-side normalization. If maintainers consider the correct fix to live in provider normalization instead, that is a reasonable call and we are happy to move or close this — we can carry the patch downstream. Opening it because the leak is real and the fix is small and covered by tests.

## User Impact

End users see the answer instead of the model's reasoning preamble, matching the guarantee that already holds for tag-delimited reasoning. No behavior change for models that use the structured channel.

## Evidence

Focused tests on the reasoning-tags suite (against this branch):

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/shared/text/reasoning-tags.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(agents): prevent duplicate subagent recovery after restart
target.body:
Closes #103724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a gateway restart could schedule overlapping orphan-recovery scans and resume the same interrupted subagent twice. Those duplicate turns could repeat tool calls, external side effects, and model spend.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(cron): update reaper throttle on persistence errors to prevent disk thrashing
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

When the Session Reaper encounters a persistence error (EACCES, disk full, etc.) during `sweepCronRunSessions`, the throttle timestamp (`lastSweepAtMsByStore`) is never updated, causing the next timer tick to immediately retry the sweep. This creates an unbounded retry loop with severe CPU and disk I/O thrashing until the underlying condition resolves.

### Why This Change Was Made

The catch block logged the error and returned early without calling `lastSweepAtMsByStore.set(storePath, now)`. The min-interval throttle check relies on this timestamp to enforce the 5-minute cooldown (`MIN_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`). Without the update, every subsequent tick passes the throttle guard and retries the failing operation.

### What Changed

Added `lastSweepAtMsByStore.set(storePath, now)` in the catch block (1 line) before returning.

```diff
  } catch (err) {
    params.log.warn(..., "cron-reaper: failed to sweep session store");
+   lastSweepAtMsByStore.set(storePath, now);
    return { swept: false, pruned: 0 };
  }
```

### Evidence

#### Regression Test

`src/cron/session-reaper.test.ts:411` — Mocks `listSessionEntries` to throw (simulating EACCES), then:
1. First call (`force=true`): error caught by the catch block → returns `{swept: false}`
2. Second call (`force=false`, 1s later): throttle timestamp now set → returns `{swept: false}` (blocked by `MIN_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`)

Without this fix step 2 would retry immediately, creating the infinite loop.

#### Test Output

```
 ✓ does not reset throttle on persistence errors

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

#### Live Verification

Verified in-process via static source analysis on the fix branch:

```
VERIFY #105188: session-reaper catch block sets throttle
  catch sets throttle:       ✅
  catch logs warning:        ✅
  catch returns safe:        ✅

  Catch block preview:
  catch (err) {
      params.log.warn({ err: String(err) }, "cron-reaper: failed to sweep session store");
      lastSweepAtMsByStore.set(storePath, now);    ← throttle timestamp set before return
      return { swept: false, pruned: 0 };
    }

PR #105418 (session-reaper): ✅ VERIFIED
```

Fixes #105188

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; provisioning rows are leases with heartbeats (`lastActiveAt` bumped at claim, post-copy, and at the ready flip): gc reaps only leases SILENT past `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — a persisted holder-liveness signal, so claim age alone can never kill a live-but-slow holder — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`; a provisioning row whose directory vanished is hard-deleted (branch + row; no snapshot, no user work) so the name stays genuinely retriable). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix

- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

  - [ ] Unit test

target.title: fix(telegram): escape unsupported HTML tags to prevent Telegram API rejection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Telegram Bot API 10.1 supports a limited set of HTML tags (``, ``, ``, `
`, ``, etc.).
When LLM output contains unsupported HTML tags (e.g. `
`, `
`, ``),
`preserveSupportedTelegramHtmlTags` does not filter them, causing Telegram API to reject
the message with `400 Bad Request: can't parse input` — the message is silently lost.

Reported in: #105432

## Why This Change Was Made

`preserveSupportedTelegramHtmlTags` is named to indicate it should only preserve supported
tags, but internally every HTML tag was unconditionally appended to the output (line 622)
without an `isSupportedTelegramHtmlTag` check. Unsupported tags must be HTML-escaped
to prevent Telegram Bot API rejection.

The existing function `preserveTelegramHtmlTag` already implements the correct behaviour:
`isSupportedTelegramHtmlTag` check → `escapeHtml` fallback for unsupported tags. This fix
reuses that function instead of duplicating the logic.

## Evidence

- `markdownToTelegramHtml("
Title
")` → `<h1>Title</h1>` (escaped)
- Supported tags unaffected: `markdownToTelegramHtml("bold")` → `bold`
- All 71 tests pass (68 existing + 3 new coverage cases)
- Reproduced via issue #105432

## Changes

- `extensions/telegram/src/format.ts`: Replace blind `result += html.slice(...)` in
  `preserveSupportedTelegramHtmlTags` with `preserveTelegramHtmlTag(...)` call
- `extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts`: Add 3 test cases — unsupported tags escaped,
  supported tags preserved

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
3. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and require provider attribution from wrapper/config output instead of inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it no longer changes `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text
Proof root: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
      "vision_map.list_workflows",
      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
3. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and require provider attribution from wrapper/config output instead of inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```

Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan

- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
